articles.title: Brain structure, function, and behavior show independent patterns of sex differences
articles.summary: A comprehensive analysis of nearly 1,000 individuals reveals that while brain structure, function, and behavior can all predict a person's biological sex, an individual's degree of sex typicality in one trait does not predict the others.

articles.title: Support for political violence drops across the board, though MAGA supporters remain the most likely to justify it
articles.summary: A new survey finds that American support for political violence decreased heading into the 2026 midterms. While MAGA supporters remain the most likely to justify violence, overall willingness to commit physical harm dropped across the ideological spectrum.

articles.title: Couples searching for a third partner report stronger bonds but often ignore the newcomer’s desires
articles.summary: Established couples seeking a third person for sexual or romantic relationships often focus on their own pleasure while ignoring the newcomer's desires. A new study explores how the search affects the original relationship and the people pursued.

articles.summary: A 10-minute jog as slow as a walk provides a measurable boost to your brain. New research shows this low-effort exercise sharpens focus, lifts mood, and activates key cognitive control centers.

articles.title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
articles.summary: A new needle-thin brain implant can record neural activity, deliver drugs, and stimulate multiple brain regions using a single flexible fiber. Successful tests in mice suggest it could give scientists a more precise, less invasive way to study the brain and may eventually help treat neurological disorders such as epilepsy.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover the human brain may actually be two separate organs
articles.summary: Scientists have found that the human brain develops from two distinct cellular systems, suggesting that evolution fused together two ancient nervous systems with very different jobs. The discovery also allowed researchers to grow human hindbrain neurons in the lab, opening new possibilities for studying ALS, spinal muscular atrophy, and other brainstem diseases.

articles.title: Scientists find that “perfect” systems may be surprisingly fragile
articles.summary: Complex systems may work better when their parts are not perfectly alike. Northwestern physicists found that carefully balanced variation, or “disorder,” can make networks such as power grids, ecosystems, neurons, and materials more stable. Even random differences sometimes improved stability compared with completely uniform systems. The discovery could help researchers design more resilient technologies and explain why natural systems are so rarely perfectly uniform.

articles.title: Scientists restore a brain protein and reverse signs of aging in mice
articles.summary: Scientists found that declining levels of the brain protein Menin may help drive aging, with lower levels in mice linked to inflammation, cognitive decline, weaker bones, and thinner skin. Restoring Menin reversed several age-related changes, while the amino acid D-serine improved cognition, hinting at a potentially intriguing new target for healthy aging.

articles.title: Does a low resting heart rate actually cause antisocial behavior?
articles.summary: Using genetic data from thousands of twins, researchers have challenged a long-held psychological theory. They found little evidence that resting heart rate causes antisocial behavior, pointing instead to sensation seeking as a key target for behavioral therapies.

articles.title: CaLR: Causal Latent Revision for Robust Diffusion Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.20981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoregressive (AR) models suffer from local greediness, while diffusion language models (DLMs) often lack the strict causal structure required for reasoning. To combine the advantages and overcome the drawbacks of the dual, we propose Causal Latent Revision (CaLR), a framework that reformulates reasoning as constrained latent optimization. By adopting a causal topology matrix (CTM) from an expert model and implicit differentiation, CaLR performs gradient-guided ``thought revision" to enforce logical consistency, enabling dynamic self-correction
